correctness.rationale: The exact four-term block-energy identity in RESULT.md is reconstructed from the full Gram expansion. When the smallest head-coordinate curvature exceeds one, nonnegativity yields an explicit positive tube coefficient. When it is smaller than one, a one-row feasible perturbation has negative quadratic term. At the exact threshold, the full constrained second variation is nonnegative; nevertheless a normalized two-coordinate head-mass transfer followed by a singleton-row perturbation lowers the loss by exactly one-half the square of the transfer parameter. The global zero-loss factor exists because the number of factor columns exceeds the number of singleton blocks. All quantifiers and the equality boundary are handled analytically. The embedded checker passes 1141 exact-rational tests, which are supplementary rather than infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Zhang's 2025 preprint (Theorem 4 and Lemma 12 in the readable 2026 journal text) establishes the balanced strictly-imbalanced-block example, which is credited and not claimed as new. The source neither states the necessary-and-sufficient smallest-coordinate threshold over every positive unit factor orientation nor classifies the equality stratum as constrained second-order stationary but nonminimizing. The new classification concerns all orientations within one continuous Gram-equivalent fiber. This is a statement and implication comparison, not a title search. The related Hayashi et al. work addresses numerical algorithms and the unconstrained Bhojanapalli et al. work addresses a different feasible cone. Published-record searches found no covering statement, but unindexed equivalences and direct extensions of the source proof remain genuine residual risks.
residual_risks: The balanced Zhang counterexample and its proof are extremely close; a different existing source may already generalize the sufficient inequality to arbitrary positive orientations.
A historical or unindexed paper might contain the full iff and equality classification under copositivity or clustering terminology.
The Hayashi and Bhojanapalli sources were only screened at abstract level; their full texts were not used to assert whole-document noncoverage.

value.rationale: The cluster-collapse example in Zhang motivates a continuous fixed-Gram family. Classifying every positive orientation into a spurious local minimum, a genuine second-order stationary yet nonminimal boundary point, or a negative-curvature saddle is a natural complete landscape classification. It exposes a consequential non-identifiability: factors with the same fitted matrix, objective, and gradient can have different constrained local geometries. The rank imbalance existence threshold and explicit entrywise stability certificate give mathematically interpretable margins. No broad algorithmic performance theorem is required for the exact natural invariant; it is not a routine numeric extension or arbitrary slice.
